title: Industrial catalog reconciliation

recommendedMapping.reason: Use names only for the primary stress run. Manufacturer codes are intentionally missing, duplicated or stale; row_id identifies fixture rows and is not a shared business identifier.

cohorts.description: Exact names and specifications; baseline controls.
Same model and specification with reordered name tokens.
Industrial abbreviations, short manufacturer names and condensed units.
German/French product vocabulary with preserved technical specifications.
Exact inch/mm, kilogram/gram and kPa/bar conversions; no physical change.
Curly punctuation, nonbreaking spaces, accented maker names and fullwidth characters.
Inserted/transposed letters in product vocabulary with preserved model data.
Brand/legal-name aliases and additional catalog wording.
Different reference variants intentionally have the same display name; full spec identifies one.
Incoming manufacturer part number is missing, while physical fields remain complete.
Different physical variants intentionally reuse a manufacturer part code.
A service kit resembles a reference item but is a different orderable product.
Same apparent item name with a different pack size; orderable SKU is not equivalent.
Similar or identical name but incompatible electrical rating.
A new revision supersedes a reference; related does not mean interchangeable.
New manufacturers/model series and physical specs absent from the reference catalog.
Same family/model wording with an incompatible physical dimension.
Variant-bearing fields and part code are omitted; either of two variants fits.
Two reference listings describe the same full physical product; choosing one row is ambiguous.
Reordering, abbreviations, Unicode, missing code and changed measurement units together.

truthDefinition: A match requires equality of the full canonical physical specification, including maker/model, dimensions, materials, electrical ratings, kit/item, packaging and revision. Equivalent measurement units do not change identity. Superseding revisions and kits are related but not equivalent. Missing variant details or duplicate equivalent reference listings are ambiguous.
measurements: Canonical dimensions are mm, mass g and pressure bar. Displayed inch/kg/kPa values are exact conversions of canonical values.
